newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt bans fishing at mercury-polluted lake.
newsitem.headline: Egypt bans fishing at mercury-polluted lake.

text.p: Egyptian authorities banned fishing in most areas of its biggest natural lake after large numbers of fish died of mercury poisoning, an official said on Wednesday.

The health ministry's laboratories tested samples from el-Manzala lake after dead fish were found floating on its surface, the General Authority for Fisheries's official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
"Mercury was found in very high and deadly rates, reaching 4,000 parts in each one million parts," the official added. "Its source is not yet known."
The lake, 150 km (90 miles) northeast of Cairo, covers 150,000 acres (60,700 hectares). It has long been plagued by industrial pollution.
Figures on the lake's fish catch were not available but families living around it rely on fishing for their livelihood.
The ban, effective from Tuesday, is indefinite and applies to the two-thirds of the lake in the Daqahliy province, the official said. Four other provinces also border the lake.
Another official said the ministry of agriculture and land reclamation was demanding the ban be applied to the whole lake.
